questions.q: How many times did Georgia change its state flag from 2001 to 2003?
questions.explanation: Georgia had three different flags in only 27 months: the 1956 flag → 2001 Barnes flag → 2003 Perdue flag. That's 2 changes.

questions.q: The Atlanta spokesman for the New South creed was
questions.explanation: Henry Grady, editor of the Atlanta Constitution, was the leading advocate of the New South philosophy promoting industrialization and reconciliation with the North.

questions.q: What happened to Leo Frank in Marietta in 1915?
options: He was pardoned by Governor John M. Slaton
He was hanged by a mob
He was chased out of town
questions.explanation: Leo Frank was kidnapped from prison and lynched by a mob in Marietta, Georgia in 1915, despite his sentence having been commuted by Governor Slaton.

questions.q: Dahlonega was
options: where the Georgia gold rush began in 1829
where the last Cherokee Indians remained in Georgia
the largest cotton-producing town in Georgia
questions.explanation: The discovery of gold near Dahlonega in 1829 sparked America's first major gold rush, predating the California gold rush by nearly two decades.

questions.q: Tomochichi was the chief of the __________ Indians.
questions.explanation: Tomochichi was the chief of the Yamacraw Indians and played a critical role in welcoming James Oglethorpe and the first Georgia colonists in 1733.

questions.q: How did World War II affect Georgia's economy?
options: More workers went on strike than ever before
The war brought federal money into the state
Many businesses closed as men entered the military
questions.explanation: WWII brought massive federal investment into Georgia through military bases, shipyards, and defense industries, transforming the state's economy.

questions.q: What happened in Camilla in 1868?
options: The Georgia General Assembly was disbanded
Women burned down a cotton mill
questions.explanation: In the Camilla Massacre of 1868, white Democrats attacked a peaceful political march of Black Republicans, killing at least a dozen people.

questions.q: The Pickrick Restaurant became infamous for a standoff over
options: protests against US involvement in the Vietnam War
questions.explanation: Lester Maddox, owner of the Pickrick Restaurant in Atlanta, violently resisted desegregation in 1964, using ax handles to drive away Black customers — and was later elected Governor.

questions.q: During the Civil War, women rioted in Valdosta because of
questions.explanation: In April 1863, women in Valdosta and other Georgia towns rioted over severe food shortages caused by the Confederate war effort depleting local food supplies.

questions.q: Were the 1996 Olympic Games the first that the city of Atlanta had bid for?
questions.explanation: No — in the 1970s, Olympic handball player Dennis Berkholtz campaigned to convince Atlanta to bid for the 1984 Games, but the city ultimately did not submit a bid.

questions.q: James Oglethorpe was a British
questions.explanation: James Oglethorpe was a British general and philanthropist who founded the colony of Georgia in 1733 and served as its first governor.

questions.q: Who founded Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport and in what year?
questions.explanation: William B. Hartsfield founded the airport in 1925 on an abandoned racetrack south of Atlanta, and served as its first commissioner.

questions.q: What was the significance of Georgia's 1956 flag change?
options: It restored the original 1879 flag design
It added the Confederate battle flag as a response to Brown v. Board of Education
It removed all Confederate symbolism from the flag
It was designed by Governor Marvin Griffin to honor Civil War veterans
questions.explanation: The Confederate battle flag was added to Georgia's state flag in 1956 as an act of 'massive resistance' to the Supreme Court's desegregation ruling in Brown v. Board of Education.

questions.q: When did CNN begin broadcasting and how many homes did it reach at launch?
questions.explanation: Ted Turner's Cable News Network (CNN) launched on June 1, 1980, reaching 1.7 million homes as the world's first 24-hour all-news cable channel.

questions.q: What film launched Georgia's modern film industry in the 1970s, and which governor created a state film commission in response?
options: Smokey and the Bandit — Governor Perdue
Driving Miss Daisy — Governor Zell Miller
Gone with the Wind — Governor Ellis Arnall
questions.explanation: Deliverance (1972), filmed along the Chattooga River in Rabun County, brought Hollywood's attention to Georgia. Governor Jimmy Carter established a state film commission in 1973 to attract more productions.

questions.q: Who was Denmark Groover and what did he admit near his death?
options: The architect of the 2001 flag; admitted it was too controversial
Governor Griffin's floor leader in 1956 who admitted anger over integration drove the flag change
A civil rights leader who admitted collaborating with segregationists
The designer of Hartsfield Airport who admitted taking bribes
questions.explanation: Denmark Groover was Governor Griffin's floor leader in 1956 who repeatedly denied racial motivation. Near death at age 79, he admitted that anger over federal integration orders had indeed been a driving factor.

questions.q: What was Ted Turner's major philanthropic achievement in 1997?
options: He donated $500 million to start the Turner Foundation for environmental conservation
He pledged $1 billion to the United Nations — the largest single private donation in UN history
He funded the Nuclear Threat Initiative with $1 billion
He donated the CNN headquarters building to Georgia Tech
questions.explanation: In 1997, Ted Turner pledged $1 billion to the United Nations, believed to be the largest single private donation in UN history at that time.

questions.q: On what date did the IOC select Atlanta as the host city for the 1996 Olympics, and where?
questions.explanation: On September 18, 1990, IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch announced Atlanta as the host city during the final vote in Tokyo.

questions.q: What are the two parts of Georgia's 2008 film tax credit?
options: 15% base credit + 5% for hiring Georgia residents
20% base credit + 10% for featuring the Georgia peach logo
questions.explanation: Governor Perdue signed a 20% base tax credit with an additional 10% credit if the production features the Georgia peach logo promoting the state.

questions.q: What is Trilith Studios and when did it open?
options: Tyler Perry's studio complex in Atlanta, opened 2006
The renamed Georgia Film School in Savannah, opened 2010
British Pinewood Studios' first U.S. location in Fayette County, opened 2013
A Universal Studios theme park in Gwinnett County, opened 2015
questions.explanation: Trilith Studios (formerly Pinewood Atlanta) was British Pinewood Studios' first U.S. location, built in Fayette County in 2013, cementing Atlanta's status as 'Hollywood of the South.'
